Build with Muse Wonder

Use Muse Wonder when capability matters more than cost per token:

  • Multi-file coding changes: make and verify changes across many files in a real repository.
  • Long-running agents: plan, delegate to sub-agents, and work through multi-hour runs with parallel tool calls.
  • Agent main loops: run the main loop of a coding agent or an agent framework, and hand lower-cost subtasks to Muse Ember.
  • Computer use: drive a desktop from screenshots with the native computer use tool.

Muse Wonder also handles image understanding, video and audio understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding. For high-volume, latency-sensitive, or cost-sensitive work, see Choose a model.

Build with Muse Spark

Use Muse Spark for agentic and coding work that needs strong reasoning at a lower cost than Muse Wonder:

  • Agent main loops: run the main loop of an agent or assistant, and hand high-volume subtasks to Muse Ember.
  • Multi-step tool loops: plan and drive tool calls across many turns.
  • Knowledge-heavy questions: answer questions that depend on broad knowledge, without a retrieval step.
  • Coding assistants: connect the coding agent you already use, or run Muse Code.

Muse Spark also handles image understanding, video and audio understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding. For complex, long-running tasks where capability matters more than cost, see Choose a model.

Versions

Muse Spark comes in three versions. All take text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, return text, and have a 1,048,576-token context window. They differ by capability:

  • Muse Spark 1.3 (muse-spark-1.3): the latest version, tuned for agentic workflows (multi-step tool, browser, and long-horizon tasks) with improved coding over 1.2. Supports all reasoning effort levels, including the "max" level for extended reasoning (not available with muse-spark-1.3-contributor). Recommended for new work.
  • Muse Spark 1.2 (muse-spark-1.2): the previous version.
  • Muse Spark 1.1 (muse-spark-1.1): the original version.
Audio input on Muse Spark 1.3

Audio understanding in Muse Spark 1.3 is not fully supported, and response quality for requests that include audio may be degraded. For audio, use Muse Spark 1.2, or Muse Voice Transcribe for dedicated speech-to-text.

muse-spark-1.3 is the default model in most code examples in these docs. The coding agents, agent frameworks, and computer use guides use muse-wonder-1.0 for long-running agentic work.

Build with Muse Ember

Use Muse Ember for bounded work that repeats many times:

  • Sub-agent tasks: run the focused coding tasks, terminal commands, and lookups that a main agent hands out.
  • Tool calls: drive tool calls inside a larger workflow, where cost and latency per call add up.
  • Routing: classify requests and send each one to the right handler or model.
  • Work across large collections: run the same task over thousands of images, files, or records, such as captioning and sorting photos, extracting fields, or classifying tickets, with many Muse Ember requests running in parallel.

Muse Ember accepts the same request body as Muse Spark, so switching most examples is a model ID change. Switch between models lists what differs. It works with computer use, image understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.

For hard single-shot coding problems, knowledge-heavy questions, or visual coding, use Muse Spark or Muse Wonder. See Choose a model.

# Create a response

Create a model response. Optionally reference a previous response by ID to continue a multi-turn conversation with server-managed state, instead of resending the full message history.

## POST /responses

Generate a model response.

### Request body

#### Content Type: application/json

[`CreateResponse`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/responses/schemas#create-response)

### Response

`HTTP 200` — OK

#### Content Type: application/json

[`Response`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/responses/schemas#response)

#### Content Type: text/event-stream

[`ResponseStreamWireEvent`](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/responses/schemas#response-stream-wire-event)

**Python (OpenAI SDK)**

```python
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MODEL_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.responses.create(
    model="muse-spark-1.3",
    input="What is the capital of France?",
)

print(response.model_dump_json(indent=2))
```

**Python (requests)**

```python
import json
import os

import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MODEL_API_KEY']}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    json={
        "model": "muse-spark-1.3",
        "input": "What is the capital of France?",
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))
```

**curl**

```shell
curl -X POST "https://api.meta.ai/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
  "model": "muse-spark-1.3",
  "input": "What is the capital of France?"
}'
```

For usage examples, `previous_response_id` patterns, and guidance on when to use the Responses API versus Chat Completions, see the [Responses](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/protocols/responses) feature page.

# Edit an image

Edit, transform, or compose one or more input images, guided by a text prompt.

With the OpenAI SDK, upload the input image(s) as `multipart/form-data` — `client.images.edit(image=..., prompt=..., model=...)`, passing a list of files to compose several inputs. Over raw HTTP you can instead send a JSON body with an `images` array of `image_url`/`file_id` items (shown below); the OpenAI SDK does not send this JSON shape.

# Segmentation with Segment Anything Model

Segment Anything Model (SAM) is Meta's segmentation model family, originally released as [open-weight research models](https://ai.meta.com/blog/segment-anything-model-3/). Its latest version, SAM 3.1, is now available on Meta Model API. Detect, segment, and follow any object in images or video. Send media and a short noun phrase such as "yellow school bus", and the model returns every match as a box and a mask. Or mark specific objects with boxes, points, or masks, and the model segments those objects and tracks them forward, backward, or both ways through a video. The box locates the object; the mask gives you the pixel region to measure or cut out.

One model handles both images and video, so you build measurement, editing, and tracking features on top of a single API. The `sam-3.1` model — the latest SAM version — segments stills and clips over `POST /v1/responses` on `https://api.meta.ai/v1`, using the same Bearer key as the rest of the API.

# Speech to text with Muse Voice Transcribe

[Muse Voice Transcribe](https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models#muse-voice-transcribe) is Meta's speech-to-text model on Meta Model API. Transcribe live audio or an existing recording, with speech-turn detection, speaker labels, and vocabulary biasing.

## Available endpoints

Both endpoints run the same model.

| Endpoint                                     | Use it for                                    | How you connect                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime`          | Live audio: voice agents, dictation, captions | WebSocket. Authenticate in the handshake frame; the `Authorization` header is ignored. |
| `POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/transcribe` | A recording you already have                  | Multipart upload. Authenticate with the `Authorization` header.                        |

```bash
curl --fail-with-body \
  'https://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/transcribe?sessionId=my-session-id' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MODEL_API_KEY" \
  -F 'request={"mode":"DIARIZATION","model":"muse-voice-transcribe-1.0","audioEncoding":"WAV"};type=application/json' \
  -F 'audio=@meeting_audio.wav'
